 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.772/2014 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Alappuzha, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 11/12/2019.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-II, Alappuzha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 22/03/2014 at about 11:30 a.m., while he was cycling through Thumpoli-Arthungal coastal road and when he reached the place by name Thumpoli junction, motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-04/AF-3238 ridden by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
The 1st respondent/rider and the 2nd respondent/ owner filed written statement denying negligence on the part of the former.

Cleetus vs Justin @ Akhil on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133115426/
2
4. The 3rd respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the offending vehicle.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A11 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,41,100/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal 2025:KER:66459 calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter a fish vendor, aged 56 years was earning 10,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 6,000/- which is low going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v. Manager,
Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are no materials to substantiate the claim regarding the monthly income.
However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra) the notional income of the claim petitioner is fixed at 9,500/- per month.
Loss of earnings 10.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the loss of earnings granted for a period of 6 months is on the lower side taking into account the nature of injuries sustained.

10.1. In the light of the injuries sustained, which include a 2025:KER:66459 fracture, in all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 10 months and hence, he can be awarded compensation at the rate of 9,500/- for a period of 10 months, that is, 9,500/-x10=
95,000/-.
Pain and Sufferings 11.
The materials on record show that he was hospitalized for a period of 10 days.
The learned counsel also draws my attention to the materials on record which would show that after the accident took place in the year 2014, he had availed treatment till 2018 in different spells.
Therefore, an amount of 45,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable taking into account the injuries sustained by him.

Cleetus vs Justin @ Akhil on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133115426/
3 Percentage of disability 12.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioner submits that though Ext.X1 disability certificate shows the percentage of disability as 15%, the Tribunal without any reasons scaled down the disability to 10%.
Therefore, he submits that in the light of the injuries sustained, the disability ought to have been fixed at least at 20%.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third 2025:KER:66459 respondent/insurer that in the light of the injuries sustained the functional disability fixed at 10% by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and does not call for any interference.

12.1. The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries- " 1. Tenderness over left spine.
2. Abrasion left buttocks, right knee.

3. Fracture T12 vertebral body."
12.2. Ext.X1 disability certificate reads thus- DISABILITY CERTIFICATE No.MR/21/19/MCHA/MACT Date: 08/08/19

Medical Board constituted as per the order of the Hon'ble Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Alappuzha OP(MV) No:
772/14

We, the members of the Medical Board, Govt. T.D.Medical College Hospital, Alappuzha have examined Sri.Cleetus, 61 yrs, S/o Peter, residing at Kochikaranveedu, Thumpoli P.O., Aryad South,
Alappuzha on 08/08/19 and found him a person with disability by reason of physical impairment following RTA on 22/03/14, having sustained:
1) Compression fracture T12 vertebral body.
As per the scale by Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment patient has 15% of permanent disability 2025:KER:66459 considering body as a whole.
The disability is temporary/ permanent in nature and progressive/partial /total degree of disability has been found as 15% (Fifteen percentage)"
The fact that the claim petitioner is a fish vendor is not seen disputed.
Therefore, taking into account the injuries sustained and the consequent disabilities sustained, I find that the functional disability can also be fixed at 15% based on Ext.X1 certificate.
Loss of amenities 13.
An amount of 75,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 10,000/- .

Taking into account the injuries sustained which include a fracture coupled with the period of Cleetus vs Justin @ Akhil on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133115426/
4 hospitalization for a period of 10 days, I find that an amount of 25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
14. The impugned Award is modified to the following extent :

Sl. Head of claim Amount Amount Modified in No. claimed Awarded by appeal Tribunal 1 Loss of earning 1,00,000/- 36,000/- 95,000/-
(9,500/-x 10 months) 2025:KER:66459

2 Transport to 25,000/- 3,000/- 3,000/-
 hospital (No  modification)
 3

Extra 10,000/- 2,000/- 2,000/-
 nourishment (No  modification)

4 Damages to 500/- 500/- 500/-
 clothing and (No  articles modification)
 5 Medical 15,000/- 1,800/- 1,800/-
 Expenses (No  modification)
 6 Partial loss of 5,000/- -- --
 earning (No  modification)
 7 Bystanders -- 3,000/- 3,000/-
 Expenses (No  modification)
 8 Pain and 1,00,000/- 20,000/- 45,000/-
 sufferings  9 Permanent 2,00,000/- 64,800/- 1,53,900/-
 disability(Loss (9,500/-
 of earning x12x9x15/100)
 power)
 10 Loss of 75,000/- 10,000/- 25,000/-
 amenities in  life  Total 5,45,500/- 1,41,100/- 3,29,200/-
 (claim limited  to 5,00,000/-)
In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,88,100/- (total compensation = 3,29,200/-, that is, 1,41,100/- granted by the Tribunal +
2025:KER:66459 1,88,100/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
The 3rd respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount,
the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law Cleetus vs Justin @ Akhil on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133115426/
5 after making deductions, if any.
The liberty given by the Tribunal to the third respondent/insurer to recover the amount from the second respondent/owner shall stand confirmed.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
